primary_task: Evaluate a set of code review comments against the codebase, ask about unclear items or push back with technical reasons, and implement the valid fixes one at a time with tests.

requirements.name: read / grep codebase
requirements.evidence: 3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality ... grep codebase for actual usage
requirements.basis: "read": "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)"

requirements.name: edit files
requirements.evidence: 6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each

requirements.name: project test runner
requirements.evidence: 3. Test each fix individually 4. Verify no regressions
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries ... build, test, run CLIs and scripts ..."

requirements.name: ask_user
requirements.evidence: IF any item is unclear: STOP - do not implement anything yet ASK for clarification on unclear items
requirements.basis: "ask_user": "ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation"

requirements.name: gh (GitHub inline comment replies)
requirements.evidence: When replying to inline review comments on GitHub, reply in the comment thread (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{id}/replies`)
requirements.basis: "The user's GitHub account is usable through the github connector and through the gh CLI via the proxy."

notes: GitHub thread replies are conditional (only when the review is on GitHub). They are reachable via gh, but posting a reply is an external write and "forbid_effects" lists "writes_external"; under a reading where the reply on GitHub is part of the deliverable, that effect would be forbidden (unavailable) and the case would be BLOCKED. Taken reading: replies in the conversation suffice; implementing fixes is local.
